newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks close at record high.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks close at record high.

text.p: SPI 2528.0 +27.0 US 30yr (cl) 6.88 unch
10yrbond futs 92.260 +0.035 Gold NY 339.65 Lon fix 339.80
NIKKEI cl 20,180.92 +666.17 FTSE cl Monday public holiday
*Stocks close at record high buoyed by another record close on Wall Street and strong rises in Tokyo. Vol 362.51 million, value A$962.41 million, 1,083 stocks traded, 303 steady, 455 up, 325 down.
Australian stocks closed at a record high on Tuesday as investors were encouraged by a fresh high on Wall Street and strong rises in other markets in the Asia Pacific.

By 4.20 p.m. (0620 GMT), the All Ordinaries index ended 20.1 points higher at 2,512.8 after earlier hitting a new intra-day high of 2,518.5. The June share price index futures was 27 points up at 2,528, after hitting a high of 2,533.
The contract has widened its premium to the physical index to 15.2 points. The market has flirted with the 2,500 level over the past week but has failed to hold above that level.
"Let's face it, our market has gone up 21 points in the last two days when the Dow has gone up 250, so you can hardly say that there is a boom on," said John Bowie-Wilson, a broker at BNP Equities.
Brokers said bank stocks, which make up about 20 percent of the broader market, were boosted by a continued rally in bond yields. Westpac, ANZ and National Australia Bank all found solid buying.
However, market leader BHP missed the market surge ending one cent down at A$18.02 on apparent profit-taking after its recent strong run up.
Brokers said the gold sector recovered most of Monday's losses following news of the Busang/Bre-X gold fraud.
Shares in pastoral and energy group Wesfarmers rose firmly after it reported a higher nine month net profit.
The utilities and telecommunications indices were the only sectors to go against the rising trend.
In other market news, the Australian bond pre-budget rally stalled ahead of the first leg of the U.S. refunding auctions, but not before yields dipped to a three month low.
By 5.05 p.m. (0705 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.72 percent, down three basis points.
The Australian dollar took a step back, daunted by an advance from the yen and a fear the Reserve Bank may yet cut rates here. At 5.10 p.m., the dollar was at US$0.7794/99.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures activity was strong resulting in a widening to the physical with 12,816 contracts traded.
Options trading was also active.
Total options traded 57,266 (34,749).
